function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time market data, so I can’t give you the exact spot price of gold for today.  For the most accurate and up‑to‑date figure, check one of the following reputable sources:

| Source | How to access |
|--------|---------------|
| **Bloomberg** | Visit Bloomberg.com → Markets → Commodities → Gold |
| **Reuters** | Go to Reuters.com → Markets → Commodities → Gold |
| **London Bullion Market Association (LBMA)** | LBMA’s official website provides daily spot prices |
| **Kitco** | Kitco.com offers live gold pricing charts |
| **Financial news apps** (e.g., CNBC, Yahoo Finance) | Search “Gold” under commodities |

These sites update the spot price of gold in U.S. dollars per troy ounce several times each trading day. If you’re looking for historical data or want to see how the price has moved over time, most of these platforms also offer charts and downloadable data.
